target.title: feat(security): audit open ingress control-plane tool exposure
target.body:
# PR: feat(security): audit open ingress control-plane tool exposure

**Branch:** `codex/audit-control-plane-exposure`  
**Commit:** `0b72cd5834`  
**Compare:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/main...hugenshen:codex/audit-control-plane-exposure?expand=1

---

## What Problem This Solves

`gateway` and `cron` are **persistent control-plane write surfaces**:

- `gateway` can apply/patch live config (`config.apply`, `config.patch`, `update.run`)
- `cron` can create scheduled jobs that survive the originating chat/task

`src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` already classifies both as high-risk / owner-only core tools, and public docs recommend denying them on untrusted surfaces:

```json5
{
  tools: {
    deny: ["gateway", "cron", "sessions_spawn", "sessions_send"],
  },
}
```

— [Control plane tools risk](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security#control-plane-tools-risk)

But the security audit had a visibility gap:

| Existing audit | What it covers | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `collectExecRuntimeFindings` (`audit.ts`) | Exec host/security, open channel + exec (`security.exposure.open_channels_with_exec`) | Does not mention `gateway` / `cron` |
| `collectRiskyToolExposureContexts` (`audit-extra.sync.ts`) | `exec`/`process` + `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` on open ingress | **Omits** control-plane tools |
| `audit-gateway-config.ts` | HTTP `gateway.tools.allow` dangerous re-enable | HTTP surface only, not agent tool reachability from open channels |

**Risk:** an operator can run `openclaw security audit`, see exec/runtime warnings, and still miss that open group/DM ingress can reach agents with `gateway` or `cron` enabled.

---

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a new exposure-matrix finding that mirrors the exec/runtime pattern:

1. Detect open inbound policies (`listOpenInboundPolicies`)
2. For each agent scope (`agents.defaults`, `agents.list.*`), resolve effective tool policies
3. If `gateway` and/or `cron` are allowed, emit a dedicated **critical** finding

This keeps control-plane reachability visible alongside existing findings:

- `security.exposure.open_groups_with_elevated`
- `security.exposure.open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs`
- **`security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane_tools`** ← new

---

## Implementation

### New collector

`collectControlPlaneToolExposureContexts(cfg)` in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.ts`:

- Reuses the same agent-context iteration + `resolveToolPolicies` + `isToolAllowedByPolicies` path as `collectRiskyToolExposureContexts`
- Checks only `gateway` and `cron` (aligned with `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS` subset most relevant to config/automation writes)
- Emits lines like:

```text
agents.defaults (profile=coding; controlPlane=[cron])
agents.list.worker (profile=none; controlPlane=[gateway, cron])
```

### New finding

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `checkId` | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane_tools` |
| `severity` | `critical` |
| `title` | Open group/DM policy with gateway/cron control-plane tools exposed |
| Trigger | Open `groupPolicy` / `dmPolicy` (incl. legacy `dm.policy`, account overrides) + at least one scope allows `gateway` or `cron` |

**Remediation text:**

> For open groups or DMs, deny control-plane tools (`gateway`, `cron`) and prefer `tools.profile="messaging"`. Tighten dmPolicy/groupPolicy to pairing or allowlist when possible.

---

## User Impact

- **Runtime:** none
- **Operators:** `openclaw security audit` may now report a new critical finding when open ingress and control-plane tools overlap
- **Expected false-positive profile:** operators who intentionally run open ingress with `tools.profile="coding"` (includes `cron`) will be flagged — that is the point

---

## Evidence

### Local proof

```sh
pnpm test src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

New/updated cases in `audit-trust-model.test.ts`:

| Case | Expect |
|---|---|
| open `groupPolicy` + `tools.profile="coding"` | critical finding; `controlPlane=[cron]` only |
| open `dmPolicy` + explicit `tools.allow=["gateway"]` | critical finding; `controlPlane=[gateway]` |
| open group + `deny: ["gateway", "cron"]` | no control-plane finding |
| `groupPolicy="allowlist"` + coding profile | no control-plane finding |

### Diff size

```
src/security/audit-extra.sync.ts          | +57
src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts  | +68
```

---

## Evidence map

| Surface | Entry point | Owner | Caller | Sibling | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open ingress exposure matrix | `collectExposureMatrixFindings` | `audit-extra.sync.ts` | `audit.ts` security audit | `collectExecRuntimeFindings`, `audit-gateway-config.ts` | `audit-trust-model.test.ts` |
| Tool policy resolution | `resolveToolPolicies` | `audit-extra.sync.ts` | control-plane collector | `collectRiskyToolExposureContexts` | existing trust-model cases |
| Control-plane tool constants | `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS` | `dangerous-tools.ts` | HTTP deny + owner checks | default HTTP deny list | policy docs |

---

## Out of Scope

- `nodes` control-plane reachability (can add later with same collector pattern)
- Security-audit reachability for non-open but permissive ingress (e.g. wildcard allowFrom) — covered partially by `security.trust_model.multi_user_heuristic`
- Docs update to `docs/cli/security.md` (can follow if maintainers want the new checkId listed)

---

## Checklist

- [x] New finding only fires on open inbound policies
- [x] Per-agent scope reporting (`agents.defaults` + `agents.list.*`)
- [x] Critical severity for persistent control-plane exposure
- [x] Regression tests for allow / deny / non-open ingress
- [ ] CI (pending after PR open)
